passage: Nursery note, Monday. From the kitchen I heard Karthik screaming and hurried in, expecting an injury. Karthik stood rooted by the sofa, red-faced, waiting for someone to come. I checked hands, feet and head. Nothing seemed wrong, but the screaming went on and I could not tell what the problem was. Only when I knelt down did I see a teddy ear behind the sofa. I lifted the teddy out. Next time I will teach Karthik to point. Kunal

qa.q: Where did Karthik stand while screaming?
What was Karthik feeling while waiting by the sofa?
qa.a: Karthik was angry and desperate to be helped, screaming in place and hoping someone would come.

qa.q: What could Karthik try in place of screaming from one spot, and why?
qa.a: Karthik could walk to Kunal and point at the sofa, because showing the problem tells an adult what is wrong much faster than noise alone.

qa.q: How does Kunal see the screaming?
qa.a: Kunal hears loud distress but cannot tell what is wrong, so Kunal fears an injury at first and searches until the teddy ear appears.

grounding: A toddler with a teddy wedged behind the sofa screams from one spot and waits, so the caregiver cannot tell what is wrong and help is late.

passage: Thomas's teddy slid behind the sofa in the house on the church lane in Pala. He poked his arm into the gap; it wouldn't reach. So he stood where he was and screamed, again and again, not moving. In the kitchen, Rajni heard it and thought he had fallen. She checked his knees, his hands, his head. Only after five minutes did she see his finger pointing at the gap.

qa.q: What was Rajni thinking when she heard the screaming?
qa.a: She was worried and alarmed, thinking he had fallen, so she checked him all over.

qa.q: What else could Thomas do next time to get help faster?
qa.a: He could walk to Rajni and pull her to the sofa or point right away, so she knows the problem is the teddy.

qa.q: How does the screaming feel from Rajni's side?
qa.a: It is frightening and confusing for her, because the noise tells her something is wrong but not what.

grounding: A toddler screams from the spot when his teddy is wedged behind the sofa, and his caregiver cannot tell what is wrong, so help is slow.

passage: Anders stood by the sofa in the Malmö flat and howled. His bear had dropped behind the cushions, into the dark crack at the back. He did not move toward anyone. He just howled. Vera ran in from the hallway, holding one boot. "Are you hurt? Anders, where does it hurt?" He howled louder. It took her a long time to notice the bear's ear poking up.

qa.q: What was Vera holding when she ran in?
What was Anders feeling as he howled louder?
qa.a: He was frustrated and upset that Vera didn't understand, and that his bear was stuck.

qa.q: What would you change first to help Anders?
qa.a: Teach him to point or lead Vera to the problem, because howling on the spot tells her something is wrong but not what.

qa.q: What is it like for Vera to hear the howl?
qa.a: It is alarming for Vera: she thinks he is hurt and searches for an injury while the real problem waits.

grounding: A toddler howls from where he stands when his bear is stuck behind the sofa, and his mother cannot tell what is wrong.
